title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: AI Wave Closes Out Hard: Nasdaq Wipes Out Into Correction
conditions.summary: Stocks had their worst day since April 2025 as traders dumped AI and chip winners, erasing Wednesday's post-election rally. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% into correction territory while the VIX spiked about 70%.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, its worst day since April 2025.
Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.52% to 24,315 and closed in correction territory.
Dow lost 1,833 points (3.44%) to 51,523.06; Russell 2000 slid 4.45% to 2,729.89.
Traders dumped this year's AI winners; the PHLX Semiconductor Index sank about 12%, erasing Wednesday's post-election rally.
Drivers cited: hedge funds locking in 2026 profits and worries a Democratic Congress could add hurdles for AI data-center buildouts.
Tech was the worst sector (about -5.5%), followed by industrials (about -5.2%); consumer defensives held up better.
The VIX jumped about 70% to 28.18, its biggest one-day jump in over two years.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000, below the ~196,000 expected and the lowest since 1969.
Q3 productivity rose 3.6% annualized vs 2.8% expected; unit labor costs fell 0.7% vs a 0.6% rise expected.
CME FedWatch odds of a December Fed hike slipped to about 70% from about 83% Wednesday; the next decision is Dec. 9.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 6 basis points to roughly 4.84%; the dollar was steady.
WTI crude rose about 2.8% to around $90.50 on uncertainty over a US-Iran deal; bitcoin fell about 5.5%.
The Bank of England raised its policy rate to 4% from 3.75%.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: MU (Micron): -17.5% — memory and chip names led the AI unwind.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): -17.3% — chipmakers hammered as the AI trade unwound.
MRVL (Marvell Technology): -16.4% — data-center chip stocks sold hard.
NVDA (Nvidia): -9.3% — semis de-risked after the midterm results.
TSLA (Tesla): -10.8% — fears of regulatory hurdles after the Democratic sweep.
APP (AppLovin): up double digits — Q3 revenue and EPS beat and a strong Q4 outlook.
LOW (Lowe's): +7.5% and HD (Home Depot): +6.5% — money rotated toward non-AI names.
CVS (CVS Health): -12.5% — among the S&P 500's worst decliners.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Qualcomm (reported Wednesday night) closed down 9.5% as phone-chip sales fell 26% and missed estimates.
Arm (reported Wednesday night) fell 13.1% despite revenue rising 27% to $1.44 billion.
AppLovin beat with Q3 revenue of $2.18 billion vs $2.07 billion expected and guided Q4 above estimates.
After the close: IREN said AI cloud revenue nearly tripled to $200 million; Akamai revenue rose 6%.
Airbnb, Lyft and IonQ also reported after the bell; after-hours moves were not yet available.

sections.title: Business News
items: Retail traders net sold about $358 million of US stocks by mid-afternoon, on track for their biggest selling day since March 2020 (Vanda Research).
Investors are questioning whether heavy AI data-center spending will earn sufficient returns.
Challenger reported October layoff announcements of about 44,000, down 71% from a year earlier.
Oil stayed in focus as the US-Iran conflict and talk of a deal kept crude swinging.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: October jobs report — forecast about +65,000 payrolls and a 4.2% unemployment rate.
Later Friday morning: University of Michigan consumer sentiment and inflation expectations.
Before the open: Charter Communications earnings.
Next week: Constellation Energy, The Trade Desk and Take-Two report Monday; Applied Materials on Nov. 12.

Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Thursday, November fifth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down over the water, and friends, that last set of the day was rough. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon hiding under the cabana deck while the big ones broke. Come on out and say good evening, Gus! [BARK]

Here's the final set. This was a gnarly wipeout for stocks. The S and P five hundred fell four point three six percent to seven thousand three hundred fifty four. The Nasdaq Composite dropped five and a half percent to twenty four thousand three hundred fifteen, and it is now in correction territory. Small caps slid four and a half percent. The Dow lost about one thousand eight hundred thirty points, or three point four percent, to fifty one thousand five hundred twenty three. That wiped out all of yesterday's post election rally and then some.

What happened? Traders unloaded this year's big A I winners. The chip index sank more than twelve percent, as hedge funds locked in profits and worried about new rules from a Democratic Congress. Tech was the worst sector, down about five and a half percent, with industrials close behind. The fear gauge, the VIX, jumped about seventy percent to twenty eight.

Now the wind and weather. The economy actually looked sturdy. Weekly jobless claims fell to one hundred eighty nine thousand, the lowest since nineteen sixty nine, and better than expected. Third quarter productivity jumped three point six percent, and labor costs fell. Traders trimmed their bets on a December rate hike to about seventy percent. The ten year Treasury yield fell about six basis points to four point eight four percent. Crude oil rose to about ninety dollars on Iran uncertainty, and bitcoin slid more than five percent.

Now the lineup. The chip Kahunas got tossed off their boards. Micron fell seventeen percent. A M D also dropped seventeen percent. Marvell lost sixteen percent, Broadcom ten percent, and Nvidia about nine percent. But one board found a clean line. AppLovin beat on sales and profit, raised its outlook, and closed up by double digits. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! [SNACK]

Over to the tide chart. Qualcomm's phone chip sales disappointed, and the stock fell about nine and a half percent. Arm grew revenue twenty seven percent, but it still dropped thirteen percent in the selloff. After the bell, Airbnb, Lyft, IonQ, Akamai and IREN reported. IREN said its A I cloud revenue nearly tripled.

Some beach talk. Retail traders sold the most stock in a single day since March twenty twenty, with no sign of dip buying. In chop like this, don't be a kook chasing every wave. A soul surfer rides it out.

Tomorrow's forecast. The big one is the October jobs report at seven thirty A M Central. The University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey follows later in the morning. Charter Communications reports before the open. Catch me on the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning. I'm stoked to see how the swell looks after this storm.
